The Schleger Line

The family story of an Austrian great-grandfather is true — except that he was your great-great-grandfather, he called himself Hungarian, and he signed his name Fr. Ch. Schleger, baker, at Bundaberg in 1886.

Compiled 19 Aug 2026 Passes 17–19 Aug 2026 (four research passes) Sources Qld State Archives · Qld BDM index · NAA · Trove · Ryerson · Matricula · Burgenland Bunch Cost $0 — free public records only

Narrative timeline · 1851 – 2026

A baker from the Hungarian border, a Cornish girl at Apple Tree Creek, and a hundred and forty years of Queensland

Every entry carries its source. Blue-shaded rows are events on the direct line to you. Grades: A primary record or contemporaneous print · B strong secondary / researcher assertion · C inference.

Era I

Origins — the border between Austria and Hungary, c.1851

c.1851
Carl Schleger is born a subject of the Kingdom of Hungary, to Carl Schleger and Katharina Frank. He will later anglicise to Francis Charles and sign "Fr. Ch." / "F. Charl." Schleger. The registrar in 1886 writes his country as Hungarian; the Bundaberg press in 1929–30 calls him "a native of Austria". Both are reconcilable if he came from the German-speaking Hungarian borderland that became Austria's Burgenland in 1921 — the Eisenstadt/Kismarton attribution offered by two family researchers — or from the Wolfsthal/Hainburg cluster just over the line, where the surname is densest today. Neither is proven. A for the parents' names and "Hungary"; B for Eisenstadt.Qld death reg C3513/1930 · Supreme Court register entry 8040 · Bundaberg Daily News & Mail 24 Jul 1929, 4 Dec 1930 · Burgenland Bunch surname list
c.1848
Mary O'Meara (O'Mara) is born in Ireland to Thade O'Mara and Johanna O'Sullivan.Qld death reg 1932 (parents named)
Era II

Arrival and the bakery years — Maryborough, Yengarie, Gympie, 1878 – 1887

1878–79
Arrival. The 1929 golden-wedding article says Frank came out on the Scottish Hero and Mary on the Highflyer, "in 1878", and that on landing he worked for Barbeler, the local baker at Maryborough, while Mary conducted a night school. The registers were read cover to cover this pass: the Scottish Hero arrived Maryborough 5 April 1879 and carries no Schleger; the Highflyer (sailed 2 Aug 1878, "over 100 days", 340 landed) has no O'Meara. As a Hungarian subject Frank was ineligible for assisted passage, so a self-paid crossing would leave no entry — the story stands unverified rather than refuted. A registers · C reconciliationTrove 283753747 · QSA DR39478, DR38582 (S13086 passenger registers), DR39476, DR38585
19 Jun 1879
Marriage at Maryborough — registered as "Carl Schlegher" and Mary O'Meara. Ten weeks after the Scottish Hero landed. AQld marriage reg C741/1879
1880–87
Baker at Maryborough (for Barbeler), then for the Messrs Cran at Yengarie, then Gympie at the time of the rush (the bakery later sold to Sam Weller), then Duncraggan and Mon Repos. Five children born in these years: Francis Morgan (21 Mar 1880, registered "Schlegher" to father Carl — the record that ties Carl and Francis Charles together as one man), Ignatius Loyola (30 May 1881), Catherine Teresa (23 Oct 1882), Barbara Ellen (27 Dec 1884), Alphonso Leo (17 Jul 1886). Trove holds not one pre-1891 Queensland newspaper mention of the family in any spelling — the bakery years left no digitised trace.Qld birth index · Trove exhaustive search (Schleger / Schlegher / Sehleger / Schlegar)
Era III

Bundaberg — citizenship, land, and the cane, 1886 – 1932

9 Sep 1886
Naturalised at Bundaberg. Oath of allegiance before Robert Johnstone P.M.; Supreme Court register of certificates entry 8040: Francis Charles Schleger · Bundaberg · Hungary · 35 · Baker · certificate issued 13 Sep 1886. Signed Fr. Ch. Schleger. NAA holds no later alien or enemy-alien file for him — he was a British subject fifteen years before Federation and thirty before the war. AQSA S57 oath · Supreme Court register p.55 · NAA nil return
1887
Land at New Bundaberg.QSA
24 Sep 1889
Applies to select Agricultural Farm 629, 90 acres, parish of Gooburrum, Booyan Road (application dated 12 Oct 1889 in his own account); takes possession 19 March 1891.QSA S14050 dead farm file AF629 (DR221448)
13 Jun 1891
Letter in his own hand to the Secretary for Public Lands: fever "wich became acute", six months without earnings, "a wife and six children to support", "please consider the circumstanzes". Signed F. Charl. Schleger. The phonetic German spellings are the only sample of his voice that survives.QSA DR221448 pp. 7–8
1892–93
AF629 forfeited for unpaid rent; a second file (US978, Bundaberg 1892–93) follows. Thereafter farmer at Burnett Heads.QSA DR221449
1889–94
Three more children at Bundaberg: Raphael Emanuel (15 Jan 1889), Mary Anne — later always Mary Bernadette — (25 Aug 1891), Clara (26 Jul 1894). Eight in all.Qld birth index
12 Mar 1903
Ignatius Loyola, aged 21, becomes a ward of the Public Curator — file "estates, mentally incapacitated persons" 75/1903, open until Dec 1910. AQSA ITM1355052 (S334, Open Access, not digitised)
1903–1921
The daughters marry: Catherine Teresa to F. G. Hoffmann (1903), Barbara Ellen to James Chalmers (1912), Mary Bernadette to David Browne O'Leary (1916), Clara to J. A. "Bert" Marshall (1921). The sons: Francis Morgan m. Mary Kelly (1908) then Mary Agnes Zunker (1921); Raphael m. Alice Habermann (1910), later Emily Alice Turner (1944).Qld marriage index · daughters' death regs C3040/1943, C97/1967, B31149/1972, C3829/1976
1911
"Schleger Bros" hold a railway lease for the Bootharh sawmill, Maryborough — first evidence of a family sawmilling business.QSA ITM3469712 (S21280, CAT 374/3/12)
4 Aug 1915
Death of Ignatius Loyola at Burnett Heads, aged 32 — by his own hand, in a barn; "in a weak state of mind for some years". Buried Bundaberg RC cemetery. The 1929 article's "one died by accident" is this. No Schleger served in the First World War. ABrisbane Courier 5 Aug 1915 (Trove 20023652) · Bundaberg Mail 5 Aug 1915 (216913781, funeral 216913797)
19 Sep 1916
Alphonso Leo marries Mary Ellen Napier (b. Eidsvold c.1890) in Brisbane B19194/1916. He farms Burnett Heads Road "from young manhood until his death", is hon. secretary of the Burnett Heads Progress Association and for years secretary of the school committee. AQld marriage index · News-Mail 9 Sep 1964 obituary (Trove 283376481)
1 Nov 1916
Frank swears a statutory declaration about his lost naturalisation certificate — "of Burnett Heads … farmer". Still alive and farming at 65.QSA DR113994 p. 107
1917–1933
Alphonso and Mary Ellen's ten: Francis Charles (1917), Valerie Mary (1918), Kevin Leo (1919), Terence Raphael (1921), Olga (1923), Delphine (1925), Alphonsus Vincent (c.1927), Maureen, Regis Margaret (1931), Bernard/Bernadine (1932/33).Qld birth index · 1951 & 1964 notices
22 Jun 1929
Golden wedding of "Mr and Mrs F. C. Schleger of New Bundaberg" (reported 24 Jul): "Mrs Schleger is from Ireland and Mr Schleger from Austria … accepting no pension, no dole — in fact to mention pension is an insult to them." Eight children, one dead by accident, twenty grandchildren.Bundaberg Daily News & Mail (Trove 283753747)
3 Dec 1930
Frank dies at St Vincent's private hospital, Bundaberg, aged 78 — "one of the oldest surviving residents of the Burnett Heads district … a native of Austria, he came out to Queensland in the year 1878". Survived by three sons (the obituary misprints Alphonso as "Alfred Leo") and four daughters. Will 160/1931, probate to son-in-law Albert James (Bert) Marshall, process engraver, New Farm; estate £633. Death registration names his parents Carl Schleger and Katharina Frank. AQld death reg C3513/1930 · News-Mail 4 Dec 1930 (Trove 283996243) · Brisbane Courier 24 Jan 1931 (21662932) · QSA ITM2832237
17 Mar 1932
Mary Schleger née O'Meara dies, aged 84, "at the residence of her daughter, Mrs J. Chalmers, New Bundaberg".Qld death reg C110/1932 · Trove 284016575
Era IV

Burnett Heads to Rockhampton — Alphonso Leo's ten, 1941 – 1964

1941–45
Three brothers in uniform, all with father Alphonso Leo, Burnett Heads, as next of kin. Francis Charles Q71857 — sugar chemist, enlisted Childers 7 Apr 1941, 101 R.M.T., released May 1942 as a reserved occupation. Kevin Leo QX43875 — L/Cpl, 113 Aust. General Transport Coy, CMF then AIF, 1,283 days' active service in Australia, discharged 7 Nov 1945 at Redbank "for cane farming". Terrence Q208478 — cane cutter, 10 Bn Volunteer Defence Corps, discharged Oct 1945 on disbandment. Cousin Lawrence Raphuel (Raphael's son) QX501472 also served. Phonse and Bernard were too young. ANAA B884 4457111 · B883 4918841 · B884 4827472 · B883 4464771 (all digitised, downloaded)
28 Aug 1943
Terence marries Olive Lillian Sutherland (1922–2021). Their daughters Wendy (Tanner) and Tricia (Green) and seven grandchildren surface only in Olive's 2021 notice — a whole branch previously unrecorded.Des Allen & Co notice via Internet Archive
1944–52
Francis Charles marries Joyce Lillian Jones, eldest daughter of Mr and Mrs T. S. Jones of 29 O'Mara Street, Mayfield (SMH engagement 17 May 1944); daughter Margaret Susanne born Belmore 1945 — the start of the Sydney line. Diploma in sugar chemistry, by 1952 managing a vegetable-oils factory in Sydney; flies Qantas to England, Germany, Holland, America and Fiji that year.News-Mail 30 Jul 1952 (Trove 284068496)
22 Jan 1950
Valerie Mary is professed with the Rockhampton Sisters of Mercy as Sister Mary Scholastica, one of "The Nine"; at Barcaldine by 1964. B
6 Jan 1951
Engagement announced: Yola Rose, youngest daughter of Mr and Mrs F. J. Johnstone, 140 Archer St Rockhampton, to Alphonsus Vincent (Phonse) Schleger, Sydney, fourth son of Mr and Mrs A. L. Schleger, Burnett Heads Road, Bundaberg. Married later in 1951 (the Qld index stops at 1949; no marriage notice exists in Trove). AMorning Bulletin 6 Jan 1951 (Trove 57064913) · News-Mail 10 Jan 1951 (283572776)
2 Jul 1951
Mary Ellen Schleger née Napier dies at the Mater, West Bundaberg, aged 61.News-Mail 3 Jul 1951 (Trove 283510756)
8 Dec 1952
"SCHLEGER. — At Lady Goodwin, on December 8, to Phonse and Rose (nee Johnstone), a Son, Dean Michael." Your father is born in Rockhampton. AMorning Bulletin 11 Dec 1952 (Trove 57308947) · News-Mail 13 Dec 1952 (283529814)
21 Apr 1953
Regis Margaret, youngest daughter, engaged to Kevin Allan Dennien of South Bundaberg.Trove 283609352
Aug 1959
"Mr A. V. Schleger and family returned to Rockhampton after a fortnight's holiday with his father, Mr A. L. Schleger, Burnett Heads."News-Mail 29 Aug 1959 (Trove 284099083)
Nov 1963
Phonse resigns from the CSIRO to stand for the Democratic Labor Party in Capricornia. Result: Gray (ALP) 19,673 · South (Lib) 12,760 · Schleger (DLP) 3,772. He stands again in 1966 (2,967 votes). Alphonso Leo dies at the Mater, West Bundaberg, aged 78 — "the fifth child of Mr and Mrs F. C. Schleger, pioneer farmers at Burnett Heads"; 37 grandchildren. Nerimbera and after — 1971 to today

1971–92
Deaths of Terence (13 Mar 1971), Valerie (1980), Francis Charles (29 Jan 1988, St Ives NSW), Kevin Leo (13 Sep 1989) and Bernard Emmanuel (11 Jun 1992, at Goodna; buried in his father's plot). Phonse dies, aged 87, late of the Benevolent Home, Rockhampton, formerly Nerimbera. Buried Rockhampton Memorial Gardens, Lakes Creek — Pomegranate Grove C, 21. BRyerson Index · Find a Grave 206396254

Yola Rose dies, aged 90 (the notice ran 14 Dec — an earlier draft of this dossier took the print date for the death date). Children: Dean & Judy (Mackay), Lindsay (Bundaberg), Carmel & Noel, Veronica; twenty-one grandchildren named, including Shane. Buried with Phonse. AMorning Bulletin / myTributes 14 Dec 2019
2021–24
Olive Schleger née Sutherland dies 12 Aug 2021 aged 98 (Riverlea, Bundaberg; same grave as Terence, L2A/200). Anthony Lawrence "Tony" Schleger (1963–2022, Kingaroy; Raphael's grandson). Era VI · Johnston, Curtis & Jackson

Your grandmother's side — Biscovey, Maryborough, Apple Tree Creek, Colosseum, 1841 – 2022

1841–51
At Biscovey, St Blazey, Cornwall: William Curtis, copper miner, and Jane — born Malta — with children Emmery and Thomas (b. c.1840). Elizabeth Ann Barratt born Tywardreath, Mar q. 1841. A1851 census HO107/1906 f.211 · GRO 9/20
Dec q. 1859
Thomas Curtis, tin miner, marries Elizabeth Ann Barratt, St Austell district; Harriett Ann born the same quarter, baptised Par 29 Feb 1860. 1861 census: Thomas 21, Elizabeth 20, Harriet 1, at Biscovey. AGRO 5c/260, 5c/147 · Cornwall OPC 7843046 · RG9/1546 p.13
1863–c.1872
Landed Adelaide 1863 (Harriett aged 4); a Jane Curtis b. Adelaide 1863 to a Thomas Curtis may be theirs. In Queensland by the 1870s — the 1940 obituary says Teebar mines 1865; Elizabeth's 1908 pension claim says 36 years in Queensland (→ c.1872). BSAGHS index · QSA pension register DR56521 p.82
7 Aug 1877
George Johnston marries Harriett Ann Curtis, Maryborough. George selects 80 acres at Childers under the 1876 Act (selection 1153) — "Fernhill Farm", Apple Tree Creek. Eight children 1880–95. AC677/1877 · QSA LAN/P56 p.2744 (DR106768)
1880–98
Thomas Curtis: caretaker of the Maryborough bridge 1880; appointed ranger and bailiff of Crown lands April 1883; Crown Lands Ranger for Gladstone and Bundaberg (defamation suit 1886, timber prosecutions 1894–95); dies 19 Feb 1898. Elizabeth Ann d. Townsville 24 Dec 1910. ATrove 148731800, 3416966, 76384191 · C293/1898 · C4383/1911
1894–95
Fernhill Farm sold to the Isis Central Sugar Mill; CSR evicts George Johnston (Childers Police Court, 23 May 1894). He dies "rather suddenly" at Ann Street, Maryborough, 29 Mar 1895 — the inquiry hears he had been "only one week sober out of the ten months"; Harriett, 35, with eight children, takes letters of administration (£260 realty). AC2621/1895 · Trove 146969050, 146900288, 146904269, 173755765 · QSA inquest JUS/N232 132/1895
1898–1940
Harriett remarries John Hughes 1898; dies as Harriet Ann Hughes 21 Feb 1940, "Apple Tree Creek pioneer". Her children's fates: Thomas Robert Benjamin d. Gayndah 1916; Elizabeth Ann Jane (Bird, then Boge; son John Boland b. 1899) d. 1961; William John d. 1967; George Vincent d. 1967; Catherine Emily (Schmidt); Henry Albert Curtis "Gullie" d. 1928 (sons Gilbert 1925–2002, Desmond 1926–2015). A
Oct 1915
"F. J. Johnstone" on the Maryborough recruiting list 20 Oct; "left by last night's train" 27 Oct; attests Brisbane 30 Oct — held at depot, never embarks. Meanwhile a Rose Jackson of the right age is in Maryborough: Women's Patriotic Meeting volunteer Aug 1914; second in ribbon-work, Wide Bay show June 1915 — identification unproven. A / CTrove 150960055, 150957132 · 293062885, 291229410
21 Aug 1919
Frederick Jason Johnstone marries Rose Jackson. Children: John 29 Dec 1919 (d. 14 Apr 1923, aged 3), Jacquiline 10 Nov 1923, Mafalda Maria 9 Oct 1926, Yola Rose c.1929. FJ joins the railways 1922; Dallarnil 1928; ganger, Colosseum station house 1937–45, where Rose places in the Central Queensland Railway Station Gardens competition 1934, 1935, 1937, 1945. AC2254/1919 · C13851/1919, C1214/1923, C12503/1923 · Trove 55604485, 54797316, 124592159, 56441628
20 Nov 1943
Jacqueline marries L/Cpl Lawrence Aubrey Josefski, Lutheran Church, South Bundaberg — "the two bridesmaids, sisters of the bride": Mafalda, 17, and Yola Rose, 14, the earliest appearance of your grandmother in print. One child of the marriage; divorced for desertion, Rockhampton Supreme Court, Nov 1949, custody to Jacqueline — who then sings as "Jacqueline Johnstone (of Radio Fame)". AC3965/1943 · Trove 283143943, 56924082
1947–48
Family at Burnett Street, Bundaberg (1947) then Rockhampton (1948). Mafalda Maria marries Edward Lewis Bartlem (RAAF LAC, 1924–1982) 26 Jun 1948; children Jason, Devon, Adrian, Shaun, Edwina. Both sisters on stage in the "Free & Easy" revue, Bundaberg, Jan 1948. ATrove 283849360, 283358169 · C1382/1948 · Find a Grave 160442332
1969–74
Frederick Jason d. 25 Oct 1969, buried North Rockhampton Sec E Row C 20 (Presbyterian); Rose d. 12 Nov 1974, aged 81, buried beside him, Grave 22 (Roman Catholic). AC6787/1969 · C7759/1974 · Rockhampton Regional Council burial index
10 Sep 2022
Mafalda Maria Bartlem dies aged 95, North Rockhampton Cemetery Sec H Row D 5 — the last of Yola's sisters. Jacqueline's later life (any remarriage, her death, her child) is still untraced. ACouncil burial index · Find a Grave 251233434

Today. About 27 bearers of the name in Australia, nearly all Queensland, all descending from Frank and Mary: Phonse & Rose's line (Mackay, Bundaberg, SE Queensland); Kevin's and Terence's (Bundaberg — Schleger Street, Burnett Heads is named for the family); Raphael → Lawrie's (Kingaroy/Bundaberg); Frank & Joyce's Sydney line (St Ives → Central Coast). Not related: a Victorian family — C. Schleger, White Hills (Bendigo) 1856, John Schleger cellarman 1860, Alfred Francis Schleger, Melbourne 1898–1902 — in Trove decades before Carl arrived; Hans Schleger the designer (born Schlesinger); Walter Schleger the Prague-born footballer.

Your grandmother's side · Johnston(e), Curtis, Jackson

Yola Rose Johnstone's people — a Cornish miner's daughter, a Childers selector, a railway ganger, and one open question

The first pass guessed this family came from New South Wales. It didn't: the Queensland index spells them JOHNSTON, and once that was seen the whole family fell into place around Maryborough, Childers and the North Coast railway line.

Curtis — Biscovey to the Crown Lands office

Not St Austell town but Biscovey, parish of St Blazey: in 1851 William Curtis, copper miner, and his wife Jane — born Malta, which is why Thomas's Queensland death registration calls her Jane Normanton, a garrison surname present at St Blazey — with their son Thomas, 11. Thomas, a tin miner at 21, married Elizabeth Ann Barratt of Tywardreath in the last quarter of 1859; their first child Harriett Ann was born the same quarter and baptised at Par on 29 February 1860. They landed at Adelaide in 1863 and were in Queensland by the 1870s (the obituary says Teebar mines, 1865; Elizabeth's 1908 pension claim implies c.1872). In Queensland Thomas was caretaker of the Maryborough bridge, then from April 1883 Crown Lands Ranger for the Gladstone and Bundaberg districts, until he died on 19 February 1898 C293/1898. Elizabeth died at Townsville on Christmas Eve 1910 C4383/1911. Harriett's Queensland-born siblings: John (1877, one day), Frederick Thomas (d. 1879), Frederick Britton (1881–1925), William (d. 1931).

The Johnstons of Apple Tree Creek

On 7 August 1877 Harriett married George Johnston C677/1877, who had selected 80 acres at Childers under the 1876 Act — "Fernhill Farm", Apple Tree Creek, where they were "among the first settlers". Eight children followed, the seventh Frederick Jason, 28 December 1892 C12224/1893. The farm was sold to the Isis Central Sugar Mill, and in May 1894 CSR had George evicted; he moved the family to Ann Street, Maryborough, "out of business", and died there on 29 March 1895 C2621/1895 — the magisterial inquiry heard from Harriett that he had been "only one week sober out of the ten months", with delirium tremens. The identification is now proven, which fixes his parents as William Johnston & Elizabeth Vincent (a brother Robert d. 1880) — an immigrant family not married in Queensland, origin still unknown. Harriett, 35 with eight children, took letters of administration (£260), remarried John Hughes of Maryborough in 1898, and died as Harriet Ann Hughes, "Apple Tree Creek pioneer", on 21 February 1940 C856/1940.

The other children: Thomas Robert Benjamin (1880–1916, d. Gayndah); Harriet (1883, infant); Elizabeth Ann Jane (1884–1961; m. Joseph Bird 1900, Marcus Boge 1924; her son John Boland, b. 1899, was raised as a brother); William John (1886–1967); George Vincent (1888–1967); Catherine Emily (b. 1890, Mrs T. M. Schmidt); Henry Albert Curtis "Gullie" (1895–1928, railway painter, m. Elsie Daisy Strehlau; sons Gilbert Henry 1925–2002, locomotive driver, and Desmond Robert 1926–2015).

Frederick Jason "Toby" Johnstone (1892 – 1969)

Born Maryborough; a hairdresser; militia; on the Maryborough recruiting list 20 Oct 1915, attested at Brisbane on 30 Oct — 5 ft 5¾ in, fair, grey eyes, Methodist; held at a depot battalion, stamped DEPOT, never embarked. He married Rose Jackson on 21 August 1919 C2254/1919; Queensland Railways from 1922; at Dallarnil 1928; fettler, then ganger; Colosseum station house on the North Coast Line 1937–45 (No. 17 gang, Makowata, 1943); Burnett Street, Bundaberg, 1947; the Rockhampton workshops from 1948. Died 25 Oct 1969, buried North Rockhampton Cemetery, Sec E Row C 20, Presbyterian.

Rose is visible in print for the first time: "Mrs R. Johnstone, Colosseum" placed in the Central Queensland Railway Station Gardens competition in 1934, 1935, 1937 and 1945 — the credited person in that competition is usually the station master or mistress, and FJ was a ganger, so she may have held the post herself. At her eldest daughter's 1943 wedding "the bride's mother chose a floral frock of American silk". She died 12 Nov 1974, aged 81, and lies beside Frederick — Grave 22, Roman Catholic.

Yola's sisters

Four children: John (1919 – 14 Apr 1923, aged three — Yola never knew a brother); Jacqueline (b. 1923) — married L/Cpl Lawrence Aubrey Josefski, Lutheran Church South Bundaberg, 20 Nov 1943, with Mafalda (17) and Yola Rose (14) as bridesmaids; one child; divorced for desertion, Rockhampton, Nov 1949, custody to her; thereafter the soprano "Jacqueline Johnstone (of Radio Fame)" of the Rockyettes revues, 1949–53; her later life, her child, and any remarriage are untraced; Mafalda Maria (1926–2022) — schoolgirl pen-friend seeker and crossword winner from "Station House, Colosseum", State Scholarship 1941, married Edward Lewis Bartlem (RAAF, 1924–1982) 26 Jun 1948; children Jason, Devon, Adrian, Shaun and Edwina Bartlem — first cousins of your father; died 10 Sep 2022, North Rockhampton Cemetery; and Yola Rose (c.1929–2019).

Handled narrowly · what the record says and does not say

Rose Jackson and the Aboriginal-heritage question

On record A: Rose Jackson, b. c.1893, m. Frederick Jason Johnstone 1919, d. 12 Nov 1974 C7759/1974, parents recorded as "Robert Jackson" and "Millie Jackson"; buried Roman Catholic.

Searched exhaustively, not found A: no Queensland birth for a Rose Jackson to a father Robert (whole-surname sets, every variant); no Robert × Millie/Amelia marriage; no Millie Jackson death; no Rose/Millie/Robert Jackson in the Aboriginal War Census (Maryborough district), the South Sea Islander index, or the NAA. The 1902 Maryborough neglected-children "Rose Jackson, 4" and the 1897 "Jackson tragedy" are documented and excluded.

Leads, unidentified C: a Rose Jackson of the right age in Maryborough — patriotic-meeting volunteer Aug 1914, ribbon-work prize June 1915; and one live index entry, a daughter Rose born 10 Aug 1914 to a mother "Rose Jackson", no father, died next day B37002/1914 — the only Rose Jackson recorded as a mother in the whole index.

A lead, not a finding: QSA ITM732477 "JACKSON, ROSE", Chief Protector's personal files (SRS4429, file 8R/119), restricted to 2078 — still just a name in an index; nothing connects or excludes it.

Standing inference C: a mother recorded by given name plus her husband's surname, and no birth registration, is a pattern seen in Aboriginal families in 1890s Queensland — and, the same index shows, in 36 other Jackson births 1885–1905 regardless of ancestry. Suggestive, not probative. The free record has now been worked hard enough that it will not answer this.

Geography: everything about this family is Wide Bay–Burnett (Maryborough, Childers, Dallarnil, Colosseum/Miriam Vale) until 1948 — Butchulla, Gooreng Gooreng, Gurang country, not Darumbal.

How to settle it

Two certificates — Rose's 1974 death and the 1919 marriage (birthplace, parents as stated, and any Protector's-permission endorsement, which decides it either way) — plus the cheap 1914 birth certificate B37002/1914; a free Community & Personal Histories request framed on Wide Bay and citing ITM732477 directly; and a conversation with Carmel Schleger with the corrected geography, the JOHNSTON spelling, "Toby", the Josefski marriage and Rose's garden prizes as openers.

Primary documents · Queensland State Archives & National Archives of Australia

Seven pages in their own hands

Click any document to view it large. All were retrieved free from digitised holdings; the QSA land file pages are the only surviving sample of Frank's own writing.

Where Carl came from · three hypotheses, none proven

"Hungary" on the register, "Austria" in the obituary — both can be right

The border between the two moved in 1921. A German-speaking Catholic born a Hungarian subject in 1851 in the strip that became Burgenland would be described exactly this way. But the surname today clusters just across that line, in Lower Austria. The free evidence gathered so far, side by side:

Eisenstadt / Kismarton

ForTwo independent Burgenland Bunch researchers — Cathryn King (Bundaberg) and Lynda Chalmers (Sydney) — list "Schleger, Eisenstadt, to Australia 1870s". Chalmers alone pairs SCHLEGER with FRANK, the mother's maiden name on the 1930 registration. Reconciles Hungary/Austria neatly.
AgainstNo published record behind it yet. Eisenstadt's 1857 house lists contain no Schleger; the surname appears once in all Burgenland Bunch data (Zahling, 1693). Every ANNO press hit 1840–90 for Schleger + Eisenstadt is a false positive; Hungarian free indexes are unanimously negative.
TestDiocese of Eisenstadt is not on Matricula. FamilySearch reels 004675473 (Oberberg RC 1827–70) and 004620339 (Eisenstadt town RC 1852–60) — free account. Or simply email the two researchers.
Human testimony, no record. Grade B.

Wolfsthal / Hainburg an der Donau

ForThe modern surname distribution: ~480 bearers worldwide, densest in Vienna and eastern Lower Austria, with a tight cluster at Wolfsthal/Hainburg on the Hungarian border (Josef b. c.1850, Johann b. c.1856, a WWI casualty from Wolfsthal). Schleger recurs in the Hainburg/Bruck press from 1901.
AgainstWould make Carl an Austrian subject, contradicting the 1886 register. Pre-1900 local press isn't digitised, so silence proves nothing either way.
TestEvery parish in the cluster — Wolfsthal, Hainburg, Bad Deutsch-Altenburg, Berg, Prellenkirchen, Petronell — is on Matricula, gap-free 1845–60, with bound alphabetical indexes. About 212 index images decide it, free.
Distribution and free registers, no direct evidence. Grade C.

The border villages — Kittsee, Edelstal, Deutsch Jahrndorf, Pama

ForHungarian until 1921 (so "subject of Hungary" holds), German-speaking, Catholic, and within a few kilometres of the Wolfsthal cluster (so the modern distribution holds too). Reconciles every fact at once.
AgainstNothing points to it specifically; untested.
TestNot on Matricula (Diocese of Eisenstadt); needs FamilySearch or GenTeam.at (both free-account) or the pay service matriken.at.
Untested reconciliation. Grade C.

Etymology (Digitales Familiennamenwörterbuch): a variant of Schleier (veil-maker) or of Schläger. Exact-phrase "Carl/Karl Schleger" across the whole ANNO corpus 1845–90 returns a single hit, in Prague — the name is genuinely rare in Austrian print. One apparent 1828-census "Kis-Marton SCHLEGER" was read at full resolution and is "Aaron Schlesinger" in the Jewish community list — refuted.

What is not yet proven · and how to close it

Next steps, in the order that pays

Do these

  1. Email the two Eisenstadt researchers — Lynda Chalmers (Sydney; lists Schleger and Frank) and Cathryn King (Bundaberg). Ask what the attribution rests on: a record or a story. Free, highest value.
  2. Read the Matricula "S" index pages for Hainburg, Wolfsthal, Berg, Prellenkirchen, Bad Deutsch-Altenburg and Petronell, baptisms 1845–60, plus marriage books for a Carl Schleger × Katharina Frank c.1840–50. Free, decisive for that hypothesis.
  3. Free FamilySearch account → reels 004675473 and 004620339 (the direct Eisenstadt test); free GenTeam.at account tests all three at once.
  4. Buy two certificates first: Rose Johnstone's death 1974 C7759/1974 and the 1919 marriage C2254/1919. Birthplace, age, parents as stated, and any Protector's permission. Add the cheap 1914 test: B37002/1914.
  5. Buy George Johnston's death certificate C2621/1895 (and Robert's, C1596/1880) — birthplace and years in the colony unlock the whole Johnston line; order the QSA inquest file 132/1895.
  6. Find Jacqueline's child (b. c.1944–47, Josefski) and her later life: Rockhampton press 1950–54, NAA B883 for Lawrence Aubrey Josefski (Q138061, NOK entries), the Supreme Court matrimonial file Josefski v Josefski 1949; and complete the Bartlem cousins (Jason, Devon, Adrian, Shaun, Edwina) from Rockhampton notices.
  7. GRO certificate Curtis × Barratt 1859 (5c/260) and the Qld deaths of Thomas (C293/1898) and Elizabeth Ann Curtis (C4383/1911) — settle William Barratt, the 1863-vs-1872 arrival, and Jane Normanton's Malta birth (Malta garrison chaplains' returns, TNA RG32–33).
  8. Community & Personal Histories request (Qld Government, free): Rose Jackson / Johnstone, b. c.1893, parents Robert and Millie Jackson, citing ITM732477 / 8R/119; frame around Wide Bay–Burnett (Maryborough, Childers, Dallarnil, Colosseum), not Rockhampton.
  9. Order QSA ITM1355052 (Ignatius Loyola's Public Curator file, 1903–10): medical and family correspondence, open access.
  10. Ask Carmel Schleger what the family holds, with the corrected geography and the JOHNSTON spelling in hand.
  11. Then Frank's own certificates — marriage 1879 C741/1879, death 1930 C3513/1930 — for a stated birthplace.
  12. Minor: settle Bernard Emmanual vs Bernadine Eamon; whether Kevin had a son Frank; re-run Google Books when quota resets; re-check myTributes for backfilled Rockhampton notices.

Dead ends and locked doors

  • Passenger registers — Scottish Hero 1879 and Highflyer 1878 read completely; no Schleger, no O'Meara. Consistent with self-paid passage.
  • Trove pre-1891 Maryborough/Gympie — zero hits for Schleger in any spelling. The bakery years left no digitised newspaper trace.
  • NAA — no naturalisation, alien or enemy-alien file for any Schleger; no WWI service for any Schleger.
  • DVA WWII Nominal Roll — site endpoint broken, not a paywall; everything it held was taken from the NAA files instead.
  • Death notices 1971 / 1980 / 1989 / 1992 / 2014 — coverage gaps in every free index; only cemetery data survives.
  • Sydney Morning Herald 1988/2003 (Francis Charles, Joyce) and News Corp regionals 2009/2016 — paywalled.
  • Matriken.at (pre-1852 Eisenstadt originals) — pay service. Arcanum full text — paywalled. QSA removal registers — restricted.
  • Qld marriage index stops at 1949, births at 1924 — Phonse & Rose's 1951 marriage, Jacqueline's child and any remarriage, and the Bartlem children aren't indexable online.
  • Ryerson coverage — Rockhampton Morning Bulletin indexed only Feb 1989 – Jun 2020 (so Frederick 1969, Rose 1974, Mafalda 2022 are out of scope, not absent); Maryborough/Fraser Coast Chronicle is indexed 1860–2020, which is why the Maryborough branch came out cleanly. No JOSEFSKI notices at all.
  • Qld BDM search API silently ignores parent-name filters — pull whole-surname sets and filter locally (pass 2's quoted counts were unfiltered; the conclusions held).
